title: Union of India v. Association for Democratic Reforms
summary: (2002) 5 SCC 294. Held that a voter's right to know the antecedents of a candidate is part of the right to freedom of expression under Article 19(1)(a), and directed the Election Commission to require candidates to file affidavits disclosing criminal cases, assets, liabilities and educational qualifications.

title: Lily Thomas v. Union of India
summary: (2013) 7 SCC 653. Struck down section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act 1951, under which a sitting legislator convicted of an offence could retain the seat by filing an appeal within three months. Disqualification now takes effect from the date of conviction.

title: Law Commission of India Report No. 244: Electoral Disqualifications
summary: Report chaired by Justice A. P. Shah, submitted following the Supreme Court's December 2013 directive in the Public Interest Foundation litigation on decriminalisation of politics. Examines the stage at which disqualification should be triggered and recommends that filing a false affidavit be a ground for disqualification.

title: Law Commission of India Report No. 255: Electoral Reforms
summary: Comprehensive review of electoral law covering election finance, opinion polls, paid news, anti-defection, and the conduct of elections. The reference point for most subsequent electoral-reform argument in India.

title: Law Commission Report Summary: Electoral Disqualifications
summary: A short summary of Law Commission Report No. 244 for readers who need the recommendations without the full report.
